drawn: 2026-10-18, tools/spot_check_sample.py --round3 15, on branch content after merging refinement f9ffdc4 (pass 15)
note: Text is as checked, after the round-3 fix (X-IT-9.2.3 stem). Excludes the 40 round-1 ids (ROUND1_IDS) and the 60 round-2 ids in spot-check-round2-sample.json. This file is the record of what was checked.

items.text: A user never had the budget share and wants it today. What kind of work is this?
options: Incident
A firmware change
Service request
Break/fix
items.correct: Service request
items.explanation: 1.1 — new access is a request, not a repair.

items.text: Correct order before a side panel comes off?
options: Strap over a sleeve, then pull the RAM
Defeat the ground pin so the plug fits
Power off, unplug, wait, strap on skin, open
Open the case first, then unplug it at the wall
items.correct: Power off, unplug, wait, strap on skin, open
items.explanation: Power off, unplug at the wall, wait for stored charge to drain, then put the strap on bare skin before opening: power is removed first and the strap only works against skin. Strapping over a sleeve does not ground you, and opening the case before unplugging leaves mains power and standby voltage inside. See 1.2.

items.text: A ticket says “Internet is slow.” What is the best intake improvement?
options: Escalate to the network team at once
Ask scope, start time, wired/wireless and changes
Run a speed test and close the ticket
Restart the PC first and see if it helps
items.correct: Ask scope, start time, wired/wireless and changes
items.explanation: Good intake narrows scope before any test: who, since when, wired or wireless, which apps, what changed.

items.text: What belongs in the ticket?
options: The user’s password, so the next technician can test
Your opinion of the user
Only the final fix
Facts, times, tests, next step
items.correct: Facts, times, tests, next step
items.explanation: A ticket is a shared record that many people read and keep, so it holds facts, times, tests and the next step. Writing the user’s password “so the next technician can test” exposes the credential to everyone with ticket access and breaks policy; the user resets or tests it themselves. See 1.4.

items.text: Firmware (UEFI) runs:
options: Before Windows, to check hardware and start boot
After Windows signs in, to load the device drivers
Only when the PC starts in Safe Mode
Inside Windows as a background service
items.correct: Before Windows, to check hardware and start boot
items.explanation: 2.2 — a wrong boot order looks like a dead OS.

items.text: POST code indicates graphics initialization failure; onboard video works after removing the discrete GPU. Conclusion?
options: The monitor is faulty
Onboard graphics is disabled in UEFI
The CMOS battery is flat
The discrete GPU or its power/slot path is faulty
items.correct: The discrete GPU or its power/slot path is faulty
items.explanation: Onboard video works once the discrete GPU is removed, isolating the fault to that card or its power/slot path.

items.text: About RAM does not match the DIMM count on the board. Next?
options: Treat it as seating or firmware first
Image the disk and check again
Run Windows Update, then recheck About
Disable Secure Boot and reboot
items.correct: Treat it as seating or firmware first
items.explanation: If About reports less memory than the modules you can see on the board, the usual causes are a stick that is not seated or that firmware does not detect, so check seating and firmware first. Imaging the disk or running Windows Update changes nothing about how memory is detected and only wastes the visit. See 2.6.

items.text: SMART reports rising reallocated sectors on an OS SSD; backups are current. What is the prudent plan?
options: Run a full format to remap sectors
Defragment the drive
Disable SMART monitoring
Migrate the data and replace the drive before it fails
items.correct: Migrate the data and replace the drive before it fails
items.explanation: Rising reallocations predict failure. Migrate the data and replace the drive while it still works.

items.text: A NAS reports “RAID 5 degraded”. What should happen before the failed disk is replaced?
options: Pull a second disk to test the array
Reinitialise the array to clear the error
Confirm a recent backup can be restored
Update the NAS firmware to the latest
items.correct: Confirm a recent backup can be restored
items.explanation: A degraded RAID 5 has no redundancy left; a verified backup must exist before any hands-on work.

items.text: Thermal paste was applied in a thick blob covering the entire IHS. Idle temps are high. What is the correct remediation?
options: Add more paste around the edges
Set the fans to maximum in UEFI
Clean both surfaces, apply thin paste, reseat
Replace the CPU with a cooler model
items.correct: Clean both surfaces, apply thin paste, reseat
items.explanation: Too much paste insulates. Clean both surfaces, apply a thin appropriate amount and reseat the cooler with even pressure.

items.text: POST completed and the display is dark. After checking power and input, what is the next step?
options: Swap the cable and adapter for known-good ones
Replace the graphics card with a brand-new one
Reinstall the graphics driver at once
Reset the firmware to factory defaults
items.correct: Swap the cable and adapter for known-good ones
items.explanation: The isolation order moves from the cheapest likely layer (cable, adapter) towards the graphics hardware.

items.text: Portable intake pass bar?
options: You closed the ticket quickly, without writing a note
You factory-reset the managed phone
A peer can tell from your note what to do next
You replaced the battery to be safe
items.correct: A peer can tell from your note what to do next
items.explanation: The Block 1 bar is a note a peer can act on: what you found, what you tested and what happens next. Replacing the battery “to be safe” is an unjustified change that leaves no evidence, and it is the same mistake as changing parts without testing. See 4.4.

items.text: gui-accounts on the bench is teaching you to:
options: Reset every phone the user owns
Turn off MDM so the change is allowed
Remove the work profile and then re-add it
Check who is signed in before changing it
items.correct: Check who is signed in before changing it
items.explanation: The accounts lab teaches you to check which account is signed in, and whose it is, before you change anything. Turning off MDM “so the change is allowed” removes company management to get around a control, and still does not tell you whose account you are touching. See 4.2 / 1.1.

items.text: A subnet must hold 25 hosts. Which mask is the smallest that fits?
items.explanation: A /27 (255.255.255.224) gives 32 addresses and 30 usable hosts — the smallest subnet that fits 25. A /26 fits but wastes more; /28 holds only 14.

items.text: Port 53 in ticket language?
options: Mail submit
DNS
Web
RDP
items.correct: DNS
items.explanation: TCP and UDP port 53 are DNS (RFC 1035), so a ticket mentioning port 53 is about name resolution. Mail submission uses 587, web uses 80/443 and RDP uses 3389, so naming port 53 changes your first test to a name lookup. See 5.2.

items.text: Which command shows a Windows client’s SSID, signal and authentication type?
options: ipconfig /displaydns
netsh wlan show interfaces
Get-NetIPConfiguration
netsh interface show interface
items.correct: netsh wlan show interfaces
items.explanation: netsh wlan show interfaces reports the association, signal, channel and authentication.

items.text: Task Manager shows “Virtualization: Disabled” on a host PC. Where is it turned on?
options: In the UEFI firmware settings
In Windows Update settings
In Device Manager’s CPU entry
In the Hyper-V Manager console
items.correct: In the UEFI firmware settings
items.explanation: Hardware virtualization (VT-x/AMD-V) is enabled in firmware, as a controlled change.

items.text: IaaS means you still own:
options: Nothing
The guest OS, like Chapters 2–5
Only the browser tab
The vendor’s datacenter hardware
items.correct: The guest OS, like Chapters 2–5
items.explanation: In IaaS the provider runs the physical hosts and the hypervisor, but the customer still owns the guest operating system: patching, accounts and troubleshooting work as in chapters 2–5. “Nothing” is the wrong idea that the cloud takes over all of it. See 6.2.

items.text: A VM shows Paused-Critical in Hyper-V Manager. What is the most likely cause?
options: The guest’s Windows licence has expired
The user locked the guest’s screen
The guest’s DNS settings are wrong
The host volume is almost out of space
items.correct: The host volume is almost out of space
items.explanation: Hyper-V pauses a VM when the volume holding its disks is critically low on space; the host owner must free space.

items.text: You have three theories for a fault. Which test should you normally run first?
options: The test that changes the most settings at once
The quick, safe test that could rule out the top theory
The slowest test, since it is the most thorough of them
A full reinstall, because it removes every theory in one go
items.correct: The quick, safe test that could rule out the top theory
items.explanation: Cheap, safe, decisive tests come first; a reinstall changes the system and does not reveal the cause.

items.text: An app fails for many users at one site but works for staff at home. What should you suspect first?
options: Each user’s local application cache files
A fault in every user’s home router
The site’s Internet path, proxy or DNS
The users’ keyboard and mouse drivers
items.correct: The site’s Internet path, proxy or DNS
items.explanation: Working from another network shows the service is up; the shared site path is the common factor.

items.text: Chapter 12 pass bar?
options: Password listed
Firewall off
Peer can tell the domain; safety stops held
Domains mixed together in one note with no label
items.correct: Peer can tell the domain; safety stops held
items.explanation: The chapter 12 bar is a note from which a peer can tell the domain, with every safety stop held. A listed password, a firewall left off or unlabelled mixed domains are the failures the chapter rules out. See 12.4.

items.text: You hand a ticket to the network team. What should the user hear from you before you hang up?
options: To restart the PC every hour and call back if it still fails after that
Who has it now, what is needed from them, and when the next update is
Nothing until the network team has fixed it and closed the ticket
Your best guess at the root cause, so that they feel reassured for now
items.correct: Who has it now, what is needed from them, and when the next update is
items.explanation: When you escalate, tell the user who has the ticket now, what (if anything) is needed from them, and when they will next hear. Silence and guessed causes both damage trust; restarts are not a plan.

items.text: A Windows 11 PC still boots but update files are damaged. Which option repairs it and keeps apps, files and settings?
options: Reset this PC with the Keep my files choice selected
Reinstall the current version through Windows Update
A clean install from USB media after a full backup
Remove everything, then restore the files from OneDrive
items.correct: Reinstall the current version through Windows Update
items.explanation: “Fix problems using Windows Update” reinstalls the current version and keeps apps, files and settings; Reset this PC removes apps and settings.

items.text: After enabling a host firewall, RDP to a lab VM fails though ping works. What was likely overlooked?
options: An outbound ICMP rule
Network discovery on the private profile
File and printer sharing (TCP 445)
An inbound rule for TCP 3389 (or the configured RDP port)
items.correct: An inbound rule for TCP 3389 (or the configured RDP port)
items.explanation: ICMP is allowed but the RDP port is not; the firewall needs an inbound rule for TCP 3389 (or the configured port).

items.text: Before you reboot “to clear it”:
options: Turn the firewall off to test
List processes to see what was running
Nothing, the restart clears it
Run diskpart clean on the drive to reset it
items.correct: List processes to see what was running
items.explanation: A reboot is a change that also wipes the evidence of what was running, so list processes first (Task Manager or tasklist) and record what you see. “Nothing, the restart clears it” loses that evidence; if the problem comes back, you have nothing to compare. See 8.3.

items.text: Which command lists the GPOs that applied to the computer and the signed-in user, and the ones that were filtered out?
options: gpresult /r
gpupdate /force
dsregcmd /status
w32tm /query /status
items.correct: gpresult /r
items.explanation: gpresult /r shows the Resultant Set of Policy summary for the computer and user, including the GPOs that applied and those filtered out. gpupdate /force reapplies policy; dsregcmd /status shows join state; w32tm shows time sync.

items.text: A Linux admin uses sudo -i for every task including reading logs. Better practice?
options: Share the root password with the team
Use sudo only for the commands that need it
Log in as root over SSH instead
Disable command auditing
items.correct: Use sudo only for the commands that need it
items.explanation: Use sudo only for commands that need it, ideally through specific sudo rules; a root shell for everything breaks least privilege and auditing.

items.text: A user asks you to remove the management profile from the college-owned Mac they use, because it blocks an app. What do you do?
options: Decline and send the request to the device owner
Remove it, then reinstall it after the app is set up
Wipe the Mac so that the profile is cleared away
Turn off FileVault so the app can be installed
items.correct: Decline and send the request to the device owner
items.explanation: MDM profiles enforce organisation policy; changing them is the device owner’s decision, and here the owner is the college.

items.text: What should you do with a user’s password during an access ticket?
options: Record it so tier 2 can sign in as them
Ask for it so you can test the share for them
Store it in the ticket’s private notes field
Never ask for it, type it or record it
items.correct: Never ask for it, type it or record it
items.explanation: Credentials are never shared with or stored by support; test with your own permitted accounts.

items.text: A Mac user can open files on an NTFS-formatted external drive but cannot save changes to it. What explains this?
options: macOS reads NTFS but cannot write to it without extra software
The drive is failing and the disk has switched itself to read-only
FileVault blocks writes to every external drive connected to a Mac
NTFS drives must be repaired with First Aid in Disk Utility first
items.correct: macOS reads NTFS but cannot write to it without extra software
items.explanation: macOS can read NTFS volumes but does not write to them natively; writing needs a third-party driver, or use exFAT for a drive shared between systems. Nothing in the symptom suggests failure or FileVault.

items.text: Chapter 10 pass bar?
options: Factual note, no password, Defender on
Password noted so the next tech can test
Cleaner ran with Defender paused
Firewall off until the user confirms
items.correct: Factual note, no password, Defender on
items.explanation: The chapter 10 bar is a factual note with no password in it, and Defender left on. Recording a password, pausing Defender for a cleaner or leaving the firewall off are the failures the chapter rules out. See 10.4.

items.text: USB ports on kiosks should be restricted. Which control best matches the requirement?
options: Endpoint policy blocking removable media
A UEFI password on the kiosk only
Disabling the kiosk’s Wi-Fi adapter
BitLocker on the kiosk’s system drive
items.correct: Endpoint policy blocking removable media
items.explanation: Endpoint policy blocks unauthorised removable media; physical port locks add protection where required.

items.text: An app crashes for every user after last night’s update; other apps work. What is the likely scope?
options: One user’s profile
One PC’s hardware
The building network
The app or its update, across many users
items.correct: The app or its update, across many users
items.explanation: Same app failing for everyone after a change points to the app/update, not individual PCs.

items.text: What must be in place before a rebuild?
options: Only the user’s verbal OK on the phone
The firewall turned off
Nothing beyond a reboot
A backup, a change ticket and list disk
items.correct: A backup, a change ticket and list disk
items.explanation: A rebuild destroys the OS volume, so it needs a tested backup, an approved change ticket and list disk to confirm the right disk. A verbal OK, turning the firewall off or a reboot do not protect the user’s data. See 11.3.

items.text: Which metric best indicates a storage subsystem is the bottleneck under database load?
options: High CPU with low disk latency
High network use with a short disk queue
Low memory use with a large page file
High disk latency and queue length with modest CPU
items.correct: High disk latency and queue length with modest CPU
items.explanation: High disk latency and queue length while CPU is modest show the workload is waiting on storage.

items.text: A fault disappears when the PC is started in Safe Mode. What does that point to?
options: Damage to the documents and files saved in the user’s profile
A fault in the core Windows kernel, which loads in every boot mode
A driver, service or startup program that Safe Mode does not load
Failing hardware, such as the RAM or the system disk, in the PC
items.correct: A driver, service or startup program that Safe Mode does not load
items.explanation: Safe Mode starts Windows with a minimal set of drivers and services. If the fault disappears there, something Safe Mode does not load — a driver, service or startup program — is involved; a fault that remains points at the core OS, hardware or user data.

items.text: A phishing outbreak needs a sender domain blocked within minutes. How is the change handled?
options: As a standard change with no record kept at all
As a normal change at next month’s CAB meeting
As an emergency change, reviewed after the event
As a service request from the first victim
items.correct: As an emergency change, reviewed after the event
items.explanation: Emergency changes get expedited approval by a named authority and a full review afterwards.

items.text: While fixing a PC you find files that may break the acceptable-use policy. What do you do?
options: Delete the files
Confront the user
Copy them as evidence to a USB drive
Stop and report through the policy channel
items.correct: Stop and report through the policy channel
items.explanation: Technicians follow the reporting procedure and preserve evidence as the policy directs; they do not investigate alone.

items.text: Why is a RAID 1 mirror not a backup?
options: Deletions and corruption are written to both disks
It needs twice as much power as a single disk does
It only works with hard drives, not with SSDs
It cannot be used on a computer with a TPM
items.correct: Deletions and corruption are written to both disks
items.explanation: RAID protects against a disk failure, not against deletion, corruption or ransomware.

items.text: How should the title of a knowledge-base article for a known fault be written?
options: As the name of the fix
In the user’s words, describing the symptom
As the internal problem-record number, with nothing else
In the technician’s own shorthand
items.correct: In the user’s words, describing the symptom
items.explanation: A KB title in the user’s words matches what the next technician will search for when the same symptom is reported. Problem numbers, shorthand and fix names do not match how the fault is reported.

items.text: Which PowerShell command reads the BIOS serial number now that WMIC has been removed?
options: Get-NetAdapter -Serial
Get-HotFix -Hardware -All
Get-CimInstance Win32_BIOS
Get-Process -Firmware
items.correct: Get-CimInstance Win32_BIOS
items.explanation: CIM classes still hold the hardware facts WMIC used to read; Get-CimInstance Win32_BIOS returns SerialNumber.

items.text: Which situation best justifies restarting the PC now?
options: The fault is intermittent and not seen
The user has unsaved documents open
A pending update requires a restart
No evidence has been recorded yet
items.correct: A pending update requires a restart
items.explanation: A pending restart is a documented reason; the others are reasons to wait and collect evidence first.

items.text: Which PowerShell command tests whether TCP port 443 is open on a server?
options: Resolve-DnsName server -Type 443 -DnsOnly
Get-NetAdapter server -Port 443
Get-CimInstance server -Port 443
Test-NetConnection server -Port 443
items.correct: Test-NetConnection server -Port 443
items.explanation: Test-NetConnection with -Port performs a TCP test and reports TcpTestSucceeded.

items.text: A user can ping 10.1.1.1 but not www.example.com. At which layer does the evidence point first?
options: Data link (switching)
Transport layer (TCP and UDP port numbers)
Name resolution at the application layer
Physical cabling
items.correct: Name resolution at the application layer
items.explanation: IP reachability works, so layers 1–3 are fine; failing by name points to DNS, an application-layer service.

items.text: Which IPv6 feature reduces the need for NAT as commonly used in IPv4 SOHO?
options: No need for routers
Mandatory private addressing
Enough global addresses for every device (still firewalled)
Built-in encryption that hides addresses
items.correct: Enough global addresses for every device (still firewalled)
items.explanation: IPv6 has enough global addresses for every device; firewalls, not NAT, provide protection.

items.text: Why does DNS normally use UDP for queries?
options: Queries are small and a lost one is simply retried
UDP encrypts the query
TCP cannot carry names
UDP guarantees ordered delivery of every reply packet
items.correct: Queries are small and a lost one is simply retried
items.explanation: One request and one reply fit in single datagrams; the client retries on loss. Large responses and zone transfers use TCP.

items.text: A switch receives a frame for a MAC address not in its table. What does it do?
options: Asks the router with ARP
Floods it out all ports in that VLAN except the source
Drops the frame
Sends it to the default gateway, which knows every MAC
items.correct: Floods it out all ports in that VLAN except the source
items.explanation: Unknown unicast is flooded within the VLAN; the switch learns the destination when it replies.

items.text: What happens to frames in the native VLAN on an 802.1Q trunk?
options: They get a double tag
They are sent untagged
They are encrypted
They are dropped
items.correct: They are sent untagged
items.explanation: The native VLAN is the one VLAN carried without a tag; mismatched native VLANs leak traffic between VLANs.

items.text: Single-mode fiber is preferred over multimode when?
options: Runs with low electrical interference
Connections to desktop PCs
Long runs between buildings or campuses
Short patch cords inside a rack
items.correct: Long runs between buildings or campuses
items.explanation: Single-mode carries over kilometres; multimode suits shorter in-building runs.

items.text: Wi-Fi 6 (802.11ax) OFDMA primarily improves?
options: Efficiency serving many clients at once in dense areas
Maximum range for one client
Compatibility with 802.11b clients
Encryption strength
items.correct: Efficiency serving many clients at once in dense areas
items.explanation: OFDMA divides a channel into resource units so the AP serves several clients in one transmission — efficiency in dense areas.

items.text: Which DHCP option gives clients their default gateway?
options: Option 51 (lease time)
Option 3 (router)
Option 6 (DNS servers)
Option 15 (domain name)
items.correct: Option 3 (router)
items.explanation: Option 3 lists routers (default gateway); option 6 lists DNS servers.

items.text: Many inside hosts share one public IPv4 address using different source ports. What is this called?
options: Split-horizon DNS
Port address translation (PAT)
Static one-to-one NAT
Inbound port forwarding (DNAT)
items.correct: Port address translation (PAT)
items.explanation: PAT tracks each inside flow by source port so many hosts share one address.

items.text: Which syslog severity level is more severe: 2 or 5?
options: They are equal
It depends on the vendor
2 (critical)
5 (notice)
items.correct: 2 (critical)
items.explanation: Syslog severities run 0 (emergency) to 7 (debug); lower numbers are more severe.

items.text: Which control best reduces risk of unauthorized devices on access ports?
options: A larger DHCP scope
Static IPs for known devices
802.1X port authentication
Disabling Spanning Tree
items.correct: 802.1X port authentication
items.explanation: 802.1X authenticates devices or users before the port grants access.

items.text: MTU mismatch causing PMTUD black hole typically shows up as?
options: Transfers are slow but always complete
Large transfers stall while small packets succeed
All traffic fails immediately
Only DNS fails
items.correct: Large transfers stall while small packets succeed
items.explanation: Small packets fit and succeed; large ones are dropped silently when ICMP “fragmentation needed” is blocked, so big transfers stall.

items.text: In troubleshooting methodology, changing three variables at once primarily hurts?
options: It takes longer than one change
It needs a reboot
It always causes a new outage
You cannot tell which change fixed or broke it
items.correct: You cannot tell which change fixed or broke it
items.explanation: Changing several variables at once makes it impossible to attribute the result to any one change.

items.text: A fix appears to work. How do you verify it?
options: Close the ticket when the alert clears
Ask one technician if it looks fine
Wait a week and see whether any of the affected users complain
Re-run the original failing test and confirm with affected users
items.correct: Re-run the original failing test and confirm with affected users
items.explanation: Verification repeats the test that failed and confirms the user outcome; an alert clearing is not proof.

items.text: Which command verifies which VLANs are allowed and active on a trunk?
options: show interfaces trunk
show interfaces status
show arp
show version
items.correct: show interfaces trunk
items.explanation: show interfaces trunk lists trunk ports, native VLAN, and allowed/active VLANs.

items.text: Which command adds a default route to next hop 203.0.113.1?
options: route add default 203.0.113.1
ip default-network 203.0.113.0
items.explanation: A static route to 0.0.0.0/0 via the next hop is the IOS default route. route add is a host OS command.
